scope.baseline: Previously reviewed fused small-integer DIV candidate, including all preceding optional correctness patches and dependency overrides. Before is integral-fused-2cc3024/after-bench, not the earlier native-input-cast baseline.
scope.runtime_change: Only arrow-cast 58.4.0 src/cast/mod.rs. Signed/unsigned Int8/16/32/64 to Decimal32/64/128/256 use PrimitiveArray::unary if scale is nonnegative, precision is valid for the target, and precision >= maximum integer digits + scale. Other casts retain the existing code.
scope.proof: Maximum decimal digits for Int8/UInt8, Int16/UInt16, Int32/UInt32, Int64 and UInt64 are 3, 5, 10, 19 and 20. With nonnegative scale and enough target precision, every source value fits after scaling. This also covers arbitrary values stored under NULL slots.
scope.allocation_change: Still one Decimal result values buffer. Unary avoids zeroing that buffer and per-row overflow checks; for safe casts it also reuses the input null bitmap instead of building a fresh one. Result-buffer release still uses the default allocator.

findings: The original wrapped queries run faster with the local Arrow cast candidate. Default process medians improve by about 58% and 60% for the SMALLINT literal and BIGINT targets; fixed-threshold diagnostics preserve the gain.
Execution instruction totals fall about 68% and 79% for those two wrapped queries. The optimized cast removes real computation without changing their SQL, rows, NULL counts, types or physical plans.

Native-output DIV controls have nearly unchanged instruction totals; their elapsed medians range from +0.11% to +1.05%, while the unchanged Decimal control is -0.45%. The wrapped speedup belongs to integer-to-Decimal conversion, not integer division itself.

Each target retains two high-fault candidate processes out of 12: about 5.5-5.7 ms versus about 2.5 ms in the low-fault group. Candidate syscall traces still show 2304 brk calls for 1152 batches and repeated 196608-byte heap contractions.
The patch does not fix allocator trimming. It is a local cast optimization; fixed allocator thresholds are diagnostic and cannot be reported as a production fix.
limitations: All 126 tracked Spark differences remain. The numeric oracle checks values, types and coarse error stages; full structured error equivalence is not claimed. Four multi-error queries report a different failing input first, with the same cast failure and stage; complete messages are retained.
Timing modes depend on process heap state. These sample frequencies are not production probabilities. Slow samples and earlier artifacts are retained.

User-space counters omit kernel execution costs. The host is not isolated and CPU frequency is not fixed. Native-control changes around 1% are recorded and do not establish zero overhead in every query.
This in-memory experiment does not measure Delta I/O, concurrent sessions or Python/Arrow C Stream consumption. It does not choose the embedding process allocator policy.

No global allocator, reusable-buffer pool or query-shape special case is introduced. Applying the optional candidate needs an arrow-cast path override; the default project continues using its unchanged dependencies.
